findings.source_quote: καὶ κλοπῇ οὐδεὶς ἐπὶ τῇ ἑαυτοῦ κολάσει ἥδεται.
findings.english_quote: and no one takes pleasure in theft when it means his own punishment.
findings.issue: The draft makes theft the object of pleasure and presents one's own punishment as a conditional consequence. The more source-transparent construction makes one's own κολάσει the object or occasion of pleasure, with κλοπῇ specifying its setting or means. The draft's attachment is possible, since ἥδεται can take a dative, but this materially interpretive choice is not explained. Nor do the notes address whether κολάσει here denotes punishment associated with theft or the suffering inflicted through theft. The neighboring appeal to unwillingness to suffer murder makes the latter alternative contextually important.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the draft explicitly with: “and, in the case of theft, no one takes pleasure in his own punishment.” Prefer wording that keeps one's own punishment or suffering directly attached to “takes pleasure,” and add a source-quoted note explaining the attachment and the contextual alternative “suffering through theft,” without identifying the person as either thief or victim unless justified. Any replacement requires fresh review; this is an interpretive revision, not a source-verification block.
